key_insight: A large pretrained video generation model (Cosmos‑Predict2) can be directly fine‑tuned into an effective visuomotor policy without multi‑stage post‑training or new architectural modules, leveraging its spatiotemporal priors for control and planning.
problem_solved: Reduces complexity and engineering overhead in adapting powerful video prediction models for robotics: removes the need for multiple post‑training stages and bespoke action‑generation components while retaining strong temporal understanding for control.
method: Start from a pretrained video prediction model (Cosmos‑Predict2) and fine‑tune it end‑to‑end to produce action‑conditioned predictions relevant to control tasks.
Use simple conditioning and supervision (e.g., action tokens or concatenated action inputs + imitation/planning losses) rather than adding new architectural blocks or multi‑stage training pipelines.
Leverage the model’s learned spatiotemporal priors for planning by predicting future observation sequences and selecting actions that achieve desired future states.
impact: Makes it much easier for researchers and engineers to reuse large video models for planning and control, improving sample efficiency and accelerating development of visuomotor policies without complex reengineering.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video model → lightweight action conditioning → fine‑tuned policy for control
Before/after rollouts: predicted video frames and executed robot trajectories comparing baseline vs Cosmos Policy
Bar chart: performance and sample efficiency gains vs multi‑stage or architecture‑heavy baselines
Saliency/attention map overlay on frames showing where temporal priors inform action decisions
paper_title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
paper_authors: Moo Jin Kim, Yihuai Gao, Tsung-Yi Lin, Yen-Chen Lin, Yunhao Ge
